judgments.reasoning_cat1: Permitting notices 'orally, to be confirmed promptly in writing, or by other communication' leaves the effectiveness of an unconfirmed oral notice genuinely open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Margin calls under Paragraph 4 and demands under 3(c) rely on this notice regime, while Paragraph 17 requires writings for waivers and modifications; whether an oral margin call starts the 4(c) clock is a live question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'any existing agreements between the parties containing general terms and conditions for repurchase transactions' is a limited supersession, not a full integration clause, and its reach could be argued.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Annex I ¶15 says the Agreement covers all Transactions in effect as of its date, and Annex I ¶8 expressly contemplates other agreements between the parties, which cuts against a broad supersession reading.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Assignment bar and termination-with-survival are stated definitely, including the null-and-void consequence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Subparagraph (b) carves out Paragraph 11 sums; no other provision addresses termination, so the fit is clean.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A narrow carve-out from the assignment bar; plainly worded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 15(a) and Paragraph 11; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard New York choice-of-law clause excluding renvoi; nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Annex I ¶14's New York forum selection; no competing law clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The non-waiver and written-modification rules are definite, including the express saving for delayed margin notices.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 3(a) allows oral Transaction agreements and Paragraph 13 allows oral notices, which sits in mild tension with the writing requirement here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Notice-and-representation mechanics for ERISA plan assets are specific; 'intended to be used' is the only soft phrase.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing elsewhere addresses ERISA; the paragraph is self-contained.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite condition on proceeding, though it is expressly subordinated to the discretion in (a)'s last sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 18(a) and (c); no conflict elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'no material adverse change in Seller's financial condition' is an evaluative standard, but it appears in a narrow deemed representation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Interacts with Paragraph 11(vi) (untrue representations as Events of Default) but creates no inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Statutory characterisation with express carve-outs ('except insofar as the type of Securities ... would render such definition inapplicable') that are self-qualifying rather than ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Annex I ¶10 adds a FIRREA-based recognition in the same terms; consistent with Paragraph 6's sale intent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short acknowledgement of a statutory liquidation right; nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Ties to Paragraph 11 remedies and Paragraph 19(a); coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conditional statutory characterisation, definite on its face despite the 'FDLA' typo for FDIA.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Annex I ¶9 and ¶10 address depository-institution and FIRREA matters consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Netting-contract characterisation with an express exception; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Paragraph 12 as replaced by Annex I ¶8.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A disclosure of a third party's position, not an operative obligation; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision addresses SIPA coverage.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Plain disclosure, definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 20(a) and (c).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Plain disclosure that funds are not insured deposits; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the rest of Paragraph 20 and Annex I ¶9.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It recites the Agreement as 'dated as of September 20, 1997' when the Agreement is dated September 20, 1998, and cites 'Paragraph 1' although the Applicability paragraph is unnumbered — mechanical errors in an identifying recital.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its prevailing-terms sentence is the hinge for every Annex I override (notably ¶3 reversing Paragraph 3(b) and ¶8 replacing Paragraph 12), so its reach against the body of the Agreement is directly contestable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fill-in-the-blank list answered 'None'; definite, if oddly worded given Annex II is included.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Applicability paragraph's reference to other annexes; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence restatement of intent; nothing ambiguous in itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It confirms sale characterisation while Paragraph 6 and Annex I ¶8 create deemed and express security interests, so it functions as an intent recital pointing against those operative terms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The amendment sentence is short and clear on its own terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reverses the priority rule in the printed Paragraph 3(b), so the instrument contains two flatly opposite conflict rules and a court must decide which governs a Confirmation term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The renumbering instruction is garbled ('adding in subparagraph "(a)" before the word "Seller"' and the mangled 'S(ay)'), which is a mechanical defect in an amending provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It changes the internal lettering of Paragraph 5, which is cross-referenced by 2(o) ('clause (ii) of Paragraph 5'), 3(c), 5 itself and Paragraph 8.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It uses undefined capitalised terms — 'LIBOR Rate', 'Business Day', 'Parties' — and contains a gross-up proviso capping Seller's Income Payment recovery that must be squared with the full-indemnity language preceding it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Business Day' is nowhere defined in the Agreement (which uses lower-case 'business day'), and the LIBOR-plus-1% rate sits beside Paragraph 11(h)'s greater-of-Pricing-Rate-or-Prime-Rate default interest.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'reasonably satisfactory', 'reasonably requested' and the forfeiture sentence ('will terminate payor's obligation ... to the extent') are workable but evaluative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies the gross-up in 5(b) and is consistent with it; no other provision addresses tax documentation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'substantial likelihood' is an unquantified trigger and the sub-clauses are mislettered ((i), (ii), (ii)), which obscures which limb applies.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It deems a Repurchase Date to occur by treating notice as a 3(c) demand, an acceleration route not reflected in the Repurchase Date definition in 2(q).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It uses the capitalised term 'Defaulting Party', which the Agreement never defines (Paragraph 11 uses lower-case 'defaulting party'), and refers to 'any related credit support document' although none exists here.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 11 defines Events of Default and the defaulting party in lower case, so the capitalised usage here has no defined referent in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definition of Change in Tax Law tied to a dated event; definite despite the heading being lettered '(i)' where '(f)' is intended.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently in 5(d)(2)(i); no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An inclusive definition ('includes any treaty, law, rule or regulation') which by design is open-ended but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Feeds only the Change in Tax Law definition; no tension elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'any stamp, registration, documentation or similar tax' ends in a catch-all after specifics, a mild ejusdem generis point.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used only in 5(e); consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad but standard tax definition limited to charges 'in respect of any payment under this Agreement'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 5(b), (c) and (e).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It misnames the statute ('Income and Corporations Taxes Act 1988') and conditions eligibility on Thornburg being 'a UK person or entity' when Thornburg is plainly a US corporation, leaving limb (iii) with no evident application.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its 'notwithstanding any provision' override cuts across the Applicability paragraph's broad definition of Securities and against Annex I ¶6, which addresses the alternative case that Thornburg is a U.S. person.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conditional confirmation obligation on the Agent; definite though it assumes a status ('U.S. person ... not registered as a broker-dealer') left unverified in the document.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It requires confirmation by CSFB Corporation under Paragraph 3(b), whose conflict rule Annex I ¶3 has reversed, so Agent-issued Confirmations now override the Agreement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list of Agent responsibilities miscites the rules (confirmations 'in compliance with Rule 15c3-1', a net capital rule) — a mechanical error in the enumerated duties.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with ¶6(b)(ii)'s disclaimer of Agent liability, but promises regulatory compliance duties whose breach is expressly excepted from that disclaimer.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad exculpation ('no liability ... except ... gross negligence or willful misconduct, or its failure to comply with applicable U.S. securities laws') carved by exceptions that could be read broadly against the drafter.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: CSFB Corporation is a non-signatory to the body of the Agreement yet takes rights under it, and Paragraph 10(ii) contemplates agency only if agreed in writing in advance; the arrangement must be read together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'if a price is not available from such pricing sources for particular Securities, CREDIT SUISSE FIRST BOSTON (HONG KONG) LIMITED or one of its affiliates shall be the pricing source' gives one party self-pricing power with no stated standard, and 'not available' is undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supplements the 2(j) Market Value definition that requires a source 'agreed to by the parties' and overlaps Paragraph 11(e)'s sole-discretion source selection; margin calls under Paragraph 4 turn on which controls.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'any other agreement or transaction whatsoever' and 'all transactions and agreements between them' are extremely broad catch-alls defining cross-default and setoff, and the cross-reference to 'Paragraph 11(d)()' is mangled.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It deletes and replaces Paragraph 12, expands Events of Default beyond the closed list in Paragraph 11, and grants a security interest that sits against Paragraph 6's sale characterisation and Annex I ¶2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conditional FIRREA representations with specific record-keeping duties; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Expressly additive to Paragraph 10 representations; consistent with Paragraph 19(c).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A statutory-characterisation addition mirroring 19(a), with the same self-qualifying exception.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sits with Paragraph 19(a)-(d) and Annex I ¶9; no inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'substantially the same Securities' is undefined and the notice timing ('at or prior to 10:00 am ... on such business day') has no antecedent business day, leaving the mechanic unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It creates a substitution right qualified by Buyer's veto, which must be reconciled with Paragraph 9(a)'s consent requirement and 9(b)'s deemed consent where Seller retains custody.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The foregoing amounts shall be solely determined and calculated by Buyer in good faith' is a one-sided self-calculation power with only a good-faith check, and 'loss incurred by Buyer directly arising' is open-ended.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Hedge-termination and replacement-transaction costs recoverable here must be squared with Annex I ¶13's bar on indirect, special and consequential loss.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short non-reliance representation; conventional and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Paragraph 10 representations and Paragraph 14; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL OR CONSEQUENTIAL LOSS OR DAMAGES' is a category boundary courts routinely have to draw, especially for hedge and replacement costs.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 11(h) and Annex I ¶11(d) expressly award replacement-transaction and hedge-termination costs and 'any other loss ... directly arising', so the exclusion and those recovery clauses must be harmonised.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'EXCLUSIVE JURISDICTION ... SOLELY FOR THE PURPOSE OF ANY SUIT ... BROUGHT TO ENFORCE ITS OBLIGATIONS HEREUNDER OR RELATING IN ANY WAY TO THIS AGREEMENT' mixes an exclusivity grant with a 'solely for the purpose of' limitation, which can be read as a consent-to-jurisdiction rather than a bar elsewhere.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the New York governing-law clause in Paragraph 16; nothing else addresses forum.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard, broadly worded jury waiver; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with ¶14's forum clause and Paragraph 16.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sentence sweeping in 'all Transactions in effect as of the date hereof' with no definition of which prior trades qualify or on what terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reaches back over trades made under prior arrangements that Paragraph 14 purports to supersede, so the retroactive coverage and the supersession clause must be read together.
